entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Sri. Rajesh Narayan, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that, the offence alleged in the above referred case is under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and vehemently pleaded on the necessity for a direction to dispose of the case expeditiously.

3. On a consideration of the contentions advanced, this Court is of the view that, the remedy of the petitioner is to request the same court to consider the matter expeditiously and not by seeking a direction from this Court.
The liberty of the trial court to deal with each case according to its priority cannot be entrenched upon by this Court, unless exceptional circumstances are made out.

The Constitutional courts must show restraint in issuing directions to dispose of the cases by trial courts in a time bound manner overlooking priority, as those are matters to be considered by the Trial Court themselves, unless special circumstances are made out.

However, if in case,
the petitioner makes any request to the learned Magistrate to grant priority, the same shall be considered earnestly and if priority can be accorded to the said case, the learned Magistrate will be free to consider granting such priority, notwithstanding the refusal by this Court.
With the above observations, this original petition is dismissed.
